questions.explanation: Capacity 24: +4, +3, −2 per hour. Net 5. Time = 24 ÷ 5 = 4.8 hours.

Pipe A fills a tank in 20 hours and pipe B in 30 hours. Pipe A is open for the first 10 hours, then both are open. The total time to fill the tank is
questions.explanation: A fills 1/2 in 10 hours. The remaining 1/2 at rate 1/20 + 1/30 = 1/12 takes 6 hours. Total 16 hours.

questions.question: An inlet fills a tank in 10 hours and an outlet empties it in 20 hours. Starting empty with both open, the time to fill half the tank is
questions.explanation: Net = 1/10 − 1/20 = 1/20. Half the tank takes (1/2) ÷ (1/20) = 10 hours.

questions.question: Pipe A is twice as fast as pipe B. Together they fill a tank in 12 hours. B alone takes
questions.explanation: Rates A = 2x, B = x, so 3x = 1/12 and x = 1/36. B takes 36 hours.

questions.question: Three pipes fill a tank in 10, 20 and 30 hours. Together they fill it in (to two decimal places, in hours)
An inlet fills a tank in 8 hours and an outlet empties it in 12 hours. If the tank is half full and both are opened, the time to fill it is
questions.explanation: Net = 1/8 − 1/12 = 1/24. The remaining half takes (1/2) ÷ (1/24) = 12 hours.

questions.question: A tank has two inlets that fill it in 20 and 30 hours and a leak that empties it in 60 hours. With the leak, both inlets together fill it in
Pipes A and B fill a tank in 15 and 20 hours. Both are opened, but B is closed after 6 hours. The tank is filled in a total of
questions.explanation: In 6 hours both fill 6 × (1/15 + 1/20) = 6 × 7/60 = 7/10. The remaining 3/10 by A alone takes (3/10) × 15 = 4.5 hours. Total 10.5 hours.

questions.question: A cistern is normally filled in 8 hours but takes 2 hours longer because of a leak. A full cistern would be emptied by the leak in
Pipe A fills a tank in 12 hours and pipe B empties it in 18 hours. Both are open for 6 hours, then B is closed. The time A then needs to fill the remaining tank is
questions.explanation: In 6 hours the net is 6 × (1/12 − 1/18) = 6 × 1/36 = 1/6. Remaining 5/6 by A alone takes (5/6) × 12 = 10 hours.

questions.question: Three pipes A, B and C can fill a tank in 6 hours. After working at it together for 2 hours, C is closed and A and B fill the rest in 7 hours. C alone can fill the tank in
questions.explanation: Together in 2 hours they fill 1/3. Remaining 2/3 by A and B in 7 hours: rate = 2/21. C = 1/6 − 2/21 = 7/42 − 4/42 = 3/42 = 1/14, so 14 hours.
